blind_spots_patched: Baseline Chapters 3 and 6 omitted the ₹20.64 Cr Customs Act Section 108 voluntary deposit (July 29, 2026) on UAE Palm Mid Fraction imports under India-UAE CEPA, the promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited related-party procurement structure (~₹230 Cr FY25 purchases; ₹200 Cr FY27 RPT limit pending SPA/RBI completion of the Aug 2023 ₹10 Cr buyout), and the rapid expansion from zero to 11 African/UAE subsidiaries with up to ₹350 Cr approved for Burkina Faso WOS Taang Kaam Industries SA.

Baseline Chapters 3 and 4 mentioned Sahel risk only in general terms, missing the concrete 2025–2026 West African raw shea nut export bans and levies that reshaped regional kernel trade and forced heavy local Burkina Faso capex, as well as Q2 FY27 inbound shipping/freight margin compression.

Baseline Chapter 4 compared Manorama solely against distant global parent conglomerates (AAK AB, Fuji Oil, Bunge, Wilmar, Cargill) and omitted privately held domestic Indian competitor 3F Industries Ltd. and AAK India's localized domestic manufacturing and ILLEXAO EN 10 CBE product launch.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: Founders Vinita Saraf (Chairperson & MD) and Ashish Saraf (Whole-Time Director) directly hold Board executive leadership seats guiding the ₹460 Cr capex cycle.

CONFIRMED: Cost-plus CBE conversion spread insulates operating margins in the 25%–27% band even as global cocoa prices normalize.
CONFIRMED: Mid-2026 ₹500 Cr QIP proceeds are being deployed toward the ₹460 Cr capex cycle and working-capital headroom with zero deviations.
